1.title: Exam Technique and Final Review
1.text: Welcome to Module sixteen, the last module of the course: Exam Technique and Final Review. You now know the content. This module is about turning that knowledge into points. You will learn how to pace the exam, how to read a question, how to eliminate wrong answers, how to handle multiple-response questions, and how to use your last week and your exam day. Then you will answer five practice questions about technique itself.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Pace the sixty-five questions in ninety minutes, using checkpoints. Use a four-step method for every question: read, predict, eliminate and confirm. Handle multiple-response questions, qualifier words and look-alike traps. And plan your final week, your exam day and, if you ever need it, a retake.

1.title: Case Check-In: Tidewater's Mock Exam
1.text: Tidewater's founder sat a practice exam and finished just under the pass mark. When the team reviewed the result, they found lost points, not lost knowledge. Some questions were misread. Some look-alike services were mixed up. And a few answers were left blank. The course content is covered, so now technique has to match it. Your job is to turn what you know into points.

1.title: The Exam Clock
1.text: Start with the clock. Sixty-five questions in ninety minutes is about eighty-three seconds for each question. Aim for about seventy seconds on a first pass, so the spare time is there for the hard questions. Use checkpoints as the latest point you should reach: question twenty by minute twenty-eight, question forty by minute fifty-five, and all sixty-five by minute eighty-five, which leaves a few minutes to review. Remember too that fifteen of the questions are unscored, and you cannot tell which ones, so treat every question as real. This pacing is my own guidance, not part of the exam guide. Exam tip: if you are behind at a checkpoint, answer quickly and move on, because a blank always scores zero.

1.title: Read for the Requirement
1.text: Now, reading. Read the last line of the question first, because it holds what is being asked. That tip comes from A W S's own certification blog. Then read the scenario, and underline the requirement words: most cost-effective, least operational overhead, highly available, most secure. Note the verb: record, block, detect, scan, encrypt, estimate or warn. Note the subject too: is it you or A W S, a Region or an edge location? Finally, predict the answer before you look at the options. Exam tip: the scenario is the story, and the last line is the test.

1.title: A Four-Step Answer Method
1.text: Here is a four-step method for every question. The figure shows the steps. One, read: the last line first, then the scenario. Two, predict: name the service or idea before you see the options. Three, eliminate: remove the options that are clearly wrong. Four, confirm: match the requirement word and the verb to what is left. The prediction step matters most. Exam tip: a prediction stops a plausible distractor from pulling you off course.

1.title: Eliminating Distractors
1.text: Wrong options are called distractors, and they are real services that sound plausible. So ask why each one fails. Some have the wrong job: Inspector scans, while GuardDuty detects. Some are the wrong size, with too much access, setup or cost for the need. Some have the wrong model, where you manage what A W S should manage, or the reverse. Some are half true, where one clause fits and another does not. And words such as always and never deserve a second look. Exam tip: remove two of four options, and a guess is right half the time.

1.title: Multiple-Response Questions
1.text: Multiple-response questions have two or more correct answers among five or more options. The question tells you how many to choose, for example: select two. Judge each option on its own, as true or false against the question, and then count. Choose exactly the number asked. The exam guide does not say how these questions are marked, so aim for every correct option. Exam tip: if three options seem to fit, reread the question for the word that rules one of them out.

1.title: Qualifier Words Steer the Answer
1.text: Qualifier words steer the answer. Most cost-effective means the cheapest option that still meets the need: Spot for interruptible work, Savings Plans for steady use, and cooler S three classes for rare access. Least operational overhead means managed or serverless: R D S, Lambda and Fargate. Highly available means more than one Availability Zone, with a load balancer and Auto Scaling. Lowest latency worldwide means CloudFront and edge locations. Most secure, or least privilege, means the narrowest permissions, roles instead of shared keys, and M F A. Quickly and on demand means On-Demand pricing and Auto Scaling. And decouple, buffer or fan out means S Q S, S N S and EventBridge. Exam tip: underline the qualifier, because it picks one correct answer from several that work.

1.title: Responsibility Shortcuts
1.text: Shared responsibility shows up in every domain, so keep these shortcuts. A W S is responsible for security of the cloud: the hardware, software, networking and facilities that run A W S services. You are responsible for security in the cloud: your data, who can access it, and how you configure services. Managed services shift more to A W S, so Lambda and R D S leave less to you than E C two. Shared controls, such as patching, configuration, and awareness and training, are each owned on their own side. Inherited controls come from A W S, such as physical security. Exam tip: ask who can see and configure the thing. If only A W S can, it is A W S's job.

1.title: Cost Question Shortcuts
1.text: Cost questions are pattern matching. Steady, predictable use points to Savings Plans or Reserved Instances. Flexible work that can be interrupted points to Spot Instances. Short or unpredictable use points to On-Demand. Your own licenses, or dedicated hardware, point to Dedicated Hosts. Guaranteed capacity points to On-Demand Capacity Reservations. To estimate, analyze and warn, think Pricing Calculator, Cost Explorer and Budgets. Many accounts with one bill means A W S Organizations with consolidated billing. And for data transfer, data in is free, while data out, and data across Regions, cost money. Exam tip: name the need first, then the option.

2.title: When You Are Unsure
2.text: Sometimes you will be unsure. Never leave a question blank. An unanswered question counts as wrong, and a guess has no penalty. Eliminate first, then choose between what is left. When two answers fit, prefer the one that is managed, least privilege and simplest. Take the plain reading of the question, not a clever one. Change an answer only when you find a specific reason. If the exam screen lets you mark a question to revisit, use it for the hard ones. Check the exam tutorial for how it works. A W S's pages I read do not describe that feature, so treat it as something to confirm. Exam tip: a blank always scores zero, while a guess might not.

2.title: Your Final Week
2.text: Use your final week well. Seven days out, read the current exam guide again, and check for changes. Six to four days out, redo the questions for your two weakest domains, and write your own look-alike notes. Three days out, take a timed run of about sixty-five questions in ninety minutes. A W S offers free practice sets of twenty questions. Two days out, read Module fifteen once, then say the lists aloud. The day before, do a light review, get a good night's sleep, and sort out your exam-day logistics. Exam tip: practice under the clock, because pace is a skill and it improves with repetition.

2.title: Exam Day and Afterwards
2.text: Now exam day and what follows. You take the exam at a Pearson view test center, or online with a proctor, so read the provider's rules for I D, the room and check-in. The fee is one hundred U S dollars, and a pass is valid for three years. Results are posted to your A W S Certification Account within five business days after the exam, unless they are held for review. If you do not pass, you wait fourteen calendar days. There is no limit on attempts, and each one needs the full fee. If you pass, you cannot retake the same exam for two years. As of the fourth of November, twenty twenty-six, A W S may change fees and policies, so read its pages before you book. Exam tip: check A W S's certification pages before you book.

2.title: Design Check: Tidewater's Mock Exam
2.text: Now a design check. Cover the right column and answer each row yourself. Tidewater ran short of time in the last ten questions: use checkpoints, question twenty by minute twenty-eight and question forty by minute fifty-five. They chose Inspector for detecting stolen credentials: read the verb, because detecting threats is GuardDuty. They picked one answer in a select two question: judge each option and choose exactly two. They chose the dearest option for most cost-effective: match the pricing option to the usage pattern. They left three questions blank: answer every one, because there is no penalty. And they mixed up A W S's duty and their own: ask who can see and configure it. Pause the video if you want more time.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. For pace, sixty-five questions, ninety minutes, about eighty-three seconds each, with checkpoints. For method, read the last line, predict, eliminate and confirm. For traps, watch for look-alike services, qualifier words and absolute words. For multiple response, judge each option and choose exactly the number asked. When you are unsure, never leave a blank, because there is no penalty for guessing. And plan your final week, your exam day and, if needed, a retake after fourteen days.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Tidewater needs a relational database for its order system, with the least operational overhead, and the team has no database administrators. Which option fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B, Amazon R D S. The requirement words are relational and least operational overhead. R D S is a managed relational database, so A W S handles most of the administration. E C two leaves the patching to Tidewater, S three is object storage, and ElastiCache is a cache.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Tidewater's security lead needs to find out which user deleted a security group last night. Which service records who made that A P I call? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A, A W S CloudTrail. The verb is who. CloudTrail records A P I activity, including the identity of the caller. CloudWatch shows how healthy a resource is, Config shows what changed, and GuardDuty detects threats.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Select two. Tidewater's order system runs on Amazon E C two around the clock, with steady usage that must not be interrupted. Which two purchasing options can lower the cost compared with On-Demand pricing? The five options are on the screen. The answers are B and D. Steady usage that must not be interrupted suits a commitment: Savings Plans or Reserved Instances. Spot can be interrupted, Dedicated Instances cost more for isolation, and a Capacity Reservation on its own holds capacity without a discount.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Tidewater stores customer data in Amazon R D S. Which task is still Tidewater's responsibility under the shared responsibility model? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C, deciding which users and applications can read the data. Customers are responsible for their data and for who can access it. A W S looks after the hardware, the facilities and, with a managed service such as R D S, the operating system of the database server.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. With six minutes left, Tidewater's founder has four questions unanswered and is unsure of each. Based on the exam guide's scoring rules, what should they do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D, answer all four. The exam guide says an unanswered question counts as incorrect, and there is no penalty for guessing. A guess can only help, while a blank always scores zero.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all five answers. Question one: B. Question two: A. Question three: B and D. Question four: C. Question five: D. That completes Module sixteen, and the whole course. You now have the content, the look-alikes, the chooser and the technique. Read the current exam guide once more, practice under the clock, and answer every question. Thank you for studying with us, and good luck on exam day.
